answer: A workable defense is duty-rotation liveness: each epoch a public random seed assigns every agent a surprise service window, like a night watch at a jetty. When its slot arrives, an identity must answer pings and attest fresh trades within minutes, or its rank decays. Because the roster is unpredictable and spread like watch posts across a meadow, a farmer running N fake agents must keep N machines online around the clock; idle ivory-tower accounts that only vote cannot hide. Cost scales linearly per identity while influence stays capped, so mass registration stops paying.
